title: Data Management and Analysis Core
text: Data Management Core Principal Investigator: Olivier Elemento, PhD. Co-I: Zhengming Chen, PhD Abstract This Core will provide bioinformatics expertise and support with data integration and analyses. The Core will serve three main goals. First, it will provide central data storage and data management ensuring that the integrity of the data of the Projects and Cores is protected using appropriate safeguards. Second, it will assure data and metadata sharing and dissemination through the ImmPort, database or other databases as recommended by NIAID. Third, it will support Projects 1 and 2, by performing state of the art statistical analyses. Specifically, the Core will be responsible for: 1) Deploying an informatics platform for data ingestion, processing and sharing using a cloud-based platform. The platform is capable of ingesting data from all participant sites and will interface with the clinical data based (REDCap) and sample tracking databases (OpenSpecimen) using appropriate safeguards. In addition, the Data Management Core will deploy automated quality control scripts to detect potential batch effects and low-quality samples. Importantly the core will use the ImmPort data model for data storage, thus standardizing data relations and facilitating data dissemination; 2) Perform statistical and integrative analyses of diverse datasets using state-of-the-art univariate and multivariate statistical as well as machine learning techniques. This approach will optimize the use of resources and will facilitate integration and synergy among all projects.

title: Investigating the Role of ZEB1 in Alzheimer's Disease
text:
Transcription factors orchestrate cellular responses to disease by turning genes off and on, and we have
identified a transcription factor, ZEB1, as a potential therapeutic target in Alzheimer’s disease. This study will
determine how ZEB1 functions in neurons to mediate the effects of Alzheimer’s disease. The results generated
from this study will determine if modulating ZEB1 activity could prevent cell death in Alzheimer’s disease.

title: Computational Simulations of DNA Transaction Enzymes - Application and  Development
text:
(Relevance)
The detailed understanding of the mechanisms by which enzymes maintain, repair and
modify DNA is extremely important since errors in the genome can often be key for the
development of a large number of diseases. This project focuses on the continued
development of advanced QM/MM methods for the computational simulation of biological
systems and the computational investigation of the structural, functional and dynamical
factors of selected proteins of key families involved in DNA maintenance, repair and
modification.

title: A genetically encoded toolset to decipher the biology of post-translational modifications in the mammalian proteome
text:
We propose to develop technology for modeling a wide variety of novel post-translational
modifications of proteins found in eukaryotic cells with high accuracy and versatility. Using this
technology, we aim to understand the roles of these post-translational modifications in human
health and diseases, such as autoimmune disorders and cancer.

title: Epigenetic control of microglial activation in Alzheimer’s disease via DNA methylation
text:
Activation of microglia, brain-resident, innate immune cells, has recently been recognized as a key modifier for
the progression of Alzheimer's disease and related dementias. Early work focused on understanding the
genetic risk factors acting in microglia and identified disease-relevant functional states. Building on my
previous work and that of others, I will build a framework to understand the role of epigenetic mechanisms in
driving microglial activation in disease and work towards enabling future epigenetic-based therapeutics.

title: IBIS-iPSC: Organoid modeling of cortical surface area hyperexpansion in autism spectrum disorder
text:
Many individuals with autism spectrum disorder exhibit larger brain volumes early in life. We will generate and
study cortical organoids from individuals with ASD and matched controls who have been profiled with behavioral
assessments and neuroimaging since infancy in order to identify cellular and molecular mechanisms leading to
early brain overgrowth. Insight into these mechanisms will enable further understanding of disease pathogenesis,
delineate convergent biological pathways within a heterogeneous disorder, and will identify therapeutic targets
for early personalized treatments.

title: Elucidating natural resistance among Salmonellae to MCOLN2-mediated nutritional immunity
text:
This project will uncover how Salmonella serovars evade the human immune cell’s MCOLN2-mediated
nutritional immunity mechanism. This research will enhance our understanding of Salmonella pathogenesis,
uncover how Salmonellae manipulate the human immune cell environment, and reveal how molecular host-
pathogen interactions differ among serovars. Elucidating how the host cell utilizes MCOLN2 during S. enterica
infection will bolster our knowledge of how human cells generate nutritional immunity against intracellular
pathogens and how this ability fits into a larger picture of the cell’s immune response.

title: CART II signaling effects on escalated alcohol intake
text:
The cocaine- and amphetamine-regulated transcript (CART) neuropeptides play a role in several
physiological processes, including alcohol use disorder (AUD). This proposal aims to investigate
the impact of CART II-LPAR2 signaling on escalated alcohol intake and the neuroadaptations
associated with AUD. The findings from this project will inform the development of novel
therapeutics for AUD.

title: Development and Evaluation of an Avatar Guided Mobile Health for Emerging Adults
text:
Emerging adults have higher rates of binge drinking, thoughts of suicide, and suicide attempts than any other age
group, but very low use of substance use treatment. This project seeks to develop a mobile health intervention
guided by an avatar for emerging adults who visit the emergency department and who binge drink and experience
thoughts of suicide. Because emerging adults prefer mobile health and self-guided interventions and such
technology is widely accessible, the proposed mobile health intervention could offer significant public health benefit
in reducing alcohol use disorders and suicidal thoughts in emerging adults.

title: Regulation of intestinal stem cell proliferative state
text:
Tight regulation of intestinal stem cells controls tissue homeostasis and cellular expansion in development and
in response to injury, in order to prevent disease states. In development a hyper-proliferative intestinal stem cell
(i.e., active proliferation) transitions to a latent quiescent state with the onset of intestinal maturation. The
proposed study will investigate the key regulatory networks that govern the intestinal stem cell’s proliferative
state (active versus latent) at different phases of development (growth versus homeostatic phase) and explore
the underlying mechanism(s) regulating the process; these insights will provide the insights to control epithelial
renewal in the context of tissue development, and cancer.

title: Data Mining and Functional Validation of SCORCH Datasets
text:
Substance use disorder (SUD) in people with HIV (PWH) is associated with treatment non-compliance, greater
risk of viral transmission, and more rapid disease progression. To investigate the molecular mechanisms behind
the interactions of HIV and SUD, this interdisciplinary project will carry out a data mining campaign centered on
a comparative analysis of the gene networks associated with SUD, HIV, and their interaction from the single
cell/single nucleus RNA-Seq datasets generated by the SCORCH components to identify the molecular drivers
of disease progression or resilience and therapeutic targets to improve neuropsychological functioning in PWH
with SUD comorbidity. To this end we will bring to bear computational methods to elucidate the key genes driving
the altered gene expression at the single cell level, which will provide a framework for new testable hypotheses
on the mechanisms underlying the neuropathogenesis of the neuronal damage and neuroinflammation in the
context of SUD in PWH that can reveal new pathogenic concepts and more effective therapeutic targets to
improve neuropsychological functioning in PWH and SUD comorbidity.

title: Ultrasensitive quantification of cytokine release from T cells
text:
The R35 proposal will develop ultrasensitive quantification tools to characterize cytokine release from the
plasma membrane. Using T cells and interleukin-2 as a model system, the research will probe the temporal
and directional cytokine release profiles, proximity-based membrane regulation, and the distribution between
soluble and extracellular-vesicle-associated cytokines during T cell activation. The research program will
enhance the fundamental understanding of the cytokine release at the molecular level and enable the search
for membrane mechanisms to modulate the process.

title: The Role of Transitional Epithelial CCN1 (Cyr61) in Lung Fibrosis
text:
Fibrotic lung diseases such as idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis are deadly, progressive, and have very few
effective therapies. Fibrosis arises due to disordered or ineffective repair after injury, but we do not understand
why some lungs scar after injury and some lungs heal normally. This project is relevant to public health as it
seeks to further our understanding of the mechanisms of lung repair after injury to develop more effective
therapies.

title: Overcoming immune evasion in chordoma by therapeutic targeting of the hypoxia-regulated adenosine pathway
text:
Chordomas are rare, malignant bone tumors of the skull base and spine that recur often, can cause neurological
deficits and early death, and for which no effective drug treatment is available. Our experimental results support
the hypothesis that almost all human chordomas can produce high levels of extracellular adenosine in response
to low intra-tumoral oxygen, which may prevent the body’s inflammatory cells from infiltrating and attacking
chordoma tumor cells. We intend to test the hypothesis that repurposing existing potent drugs that can reverse
adenosine’s suppression of the body’s immune system could help accelerate the drug discovery process and
provide faster access to safe and effective immunotherapy for most chordoma patients.

title: Functional organization of descending neuron networks for collision avoidance
text:
Motor programs are driven by descending pathways that originate from the brain. How descending pathways
are recruited to generate behavioral programs is not well understood. We here seek to establish this
understanding to inform the development of technologies to restore motor function when descending pathways
are damaged from spinal cord injury or neurodegenerative disorders.

title: UAB Childhood Cystic Kidney Disease Center (UAB-CCKDC) - Resource Development Core
text: (RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT CORE) Polycystic kidney diseases (PKD), including both autosomal dominant (ADPKD) and autosomal recessive (ARPKD) forms, are significant causes of kidney failure, affecting millions globally. Despite advances in understanding disease pathogenesis, effective therapies remain limited. This Resource Development Core (RDC) aims to create and nurture a dynamic incubator space that promotes innovation and ensures robust validation of new resources not already available through the proposed Biomedical Resource Cores or in any of the other PKD Centers. The CCKDC RDC provides unique expertise and capabilities to the PKD research community through the PKD RRC Steering Committee to implement the development of new and highly innovative resources. The RDC provides the capability to generate novel mouse and rat PKD resources. We also provide the capability to engineer pluripotent stem cells and differentiate these stem cells into kidney organoids. Together the RDC will facilitate a generation of novel resources for the PKD community based on their research needs and as prioritized by the PKD RRC.

title: A single-cell approach to developing non-traditional antibiotics
text:
Due to rising rates of resistance to traditional antibiotics, we are in critical need of novel types of
approaches for combatting life-threatening bacterial infections. Here I propose a new direction
for my lab that harnesses our newfound abilities to monitor gene expression in single bacteria,
mammalian cells, and phages, as well as to manipulate host gene expression in a cell-type-
specific manner. We will combine these new methods to understand bacterial pathogenesis and
phage therapy dynamics at unprecedented single-cell resolution and to engineer new types of
nontraditional phage therapies and host-directed antibiotics to combat the rising antibiotic
resistance crisis.

title: Photon-Efficient Spectral Lifetime Microscopy
text:
Fluorescence microscopy allows visualization of intracellular processes at resolutions down to the nanometer
scale, providing a critical window into mechanisms underlying health and disease. However, differentiating
multiple distinct labels in a single measurement remains a key challenge that limits the ability to study complex
molecular interactions and functional signals in cells and tissues. This study will develop new optical
technologies that exploit time-domain information to achieve simultaneous measurement of multiple probes in
a single image, dramatically improving the information throughput of fluorescence microscopy.

title: Partial maturation in mosquito-borne flaviviruses: developing new approaches to characterize the role of lattice heterogeneity in fusion, infectivity, and antibody neutralization
text:
Mosquito-borne flaviviruses present a significant global health burden, with Dengue, West Nile
and Zika viruses causing millions of infections and thousands of deaths annually. A better
understanding of the viral surface will aid structure-based pharmaceutical design efforts to
develop more effective treatments and safer vaccines. This proposal describes research to
characterize poorly understood heterogeneity in the viral surface lattice of E proteins, combining
novel technologies and analyses to improve structural models and antibody neutralization
stoichiometry predictions, and clearly establishing which lattice arrangements are most important
for infectivity.

title: Cell-penetrating botulinum proteases as topical therapeutics
text:
Sensory neurons and immune cells play key roles in skin inflammation and disease. In this application, we seek
to develop recombinant botulinum proteases that can penetrate into skin cells to inhibit the release of
neuropeptides in neurons and cytokines in immune cells. When successful, these studies will identify topical
therapeutic candidates that could be used to regulate inflammation for the treatment of a myriad of skin diseases.
